title: Bangladesh High Court Bars Hindu Monk Chinmoy Das From Bail
excerpt: Citing an active murder trial in a lower court, the High Court in Dhaka refuses to free the detained ISKCON-linked monk, now held since November 2024.
body:
Bangladesh's High Court on May 10 rejected a bail petition filed by detained Hindu monk Brahmachari Chinmoy Krishna Das, keeping him behind bars more than five months after his arrest. The court cited his ongoing trial in a lower court in connection with the 2024 killing of a lawyer as its reason for refusal.

**What happened in court:**
Das's lawyer, Apurba Kumar Bhattacharya, told reporters that 'the High Court bench rejected our bail petition as recording of witness testimony is underway in the trial court in Chattogram.' The defence had argued that Das was suffering from health ailments and had been languishing in jail without relief. An earlier High Court bail order granted on April 30 in the sedition case was subsequently stayed by the Supreme Court's apex Appellate Division.

**Why this case matters beyond Bangladesh:**
Das, a spokesperson for the Bangladesh Sammilita Sanatani Jagran Jote and a figure associated with ISKCON, was first arrested at Dhaka's Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on November 25, 2024 on sedition charges. His detention became a flashpoint in India-Bangladesh diplomatic relations, with New Delhi expressing serious concern over his treatment. Since the fall of Sheikh Hasina's government in August 2024, Bangladesh's Hindu minority — roughly 8 per cent of a 170 million population — has faced attacks across more than 50 districts, deepening anxieties about religious freedom under the interim government of Muhammad Yunus.

**What to watch next:**
Das's legal team is expected to challenge the High Court's decision further, and New Delhi's response — particularly from India's Ministry of External Affairs — will signal how much diplomatic pressure Bangladesh continues to face over minority protections.
